title: Mathematical Program Proof — collision-cert + envelope ingestion + auto-fix (JM Die fleet baseline)
summary: Mathematical machine certificate: prove via interval arithmetic + continuous swept-volume + signed-distance-field that a toolpath's tool-tip / spindle-nose envelope is strictly inside the machine's reachable + collision-free envelope at ALL parametric times. Sub-second proofs, no Vericut required. Auto-fix transforms when proof fails. Pre-emit gate guarantees user never receives an unsafe program. Baseline fleet: JM Die's 21 machines (jm-die-profile.ts JM_DIE_MACHINE_COUNT=21).
doctrine: Karpathy R5 — model only for judgment calls; deterministic safety predicates live in code, not LLM
CLAUDE.md §SAFETY — never inline constants; tier shop_floor Ω≥0.95 S(x)≥0.98

units.title: JMDieMachineEnvelopeCatalogEngine — ingest all 21 JM Die machines into a unified envelope catalog at native µm precision
scope: Per-machine: travel limits (X/Y/Z + A/B/C if 5-axis), spindle nose B-rep, table B-rep, fixture-exclusion zones (tombstone, vise, magnet), door interference, tool-holder reach cone
Source-of-truth: ShopConfigurationEngine (21 machines) + manufacturer specs + per-machine fixture catalog
Reported accuracy tier per machine: 'manufacturer-spec' (~25-50µm) | 'interferometer-cal' (sub-µm, none today) — caller knows the margin
Output: queryable catalog keyed by machine_id; signed-distance-field generator on demand
acceptance: All 21 JM Die machines have an envelope record
Per-machine record includes B-rep + accuracy tier + last-verified date
MCP-callable via prism_calc:jm_die_envelope_lookup
12+ unit tests (1 per machine class minimum), 3 adversarial (over-travel, fixture-collision, door-interference)

units.title: IntervalArithmeticPredicateEngine — wrap collision/distance predicates so FP rounding can't produce false-negatives
scope: Implement interval-arithmetic ops [add, sub, mul, div, sqrt] per Moore 1966 + outward-rounding directed-rounding semantics
Wrap distance predicates: point-in-polytope, segment-segment, swept-volume-intersect
Output bounded: 'definitely-safe' | 'definitely-collision' | 'inconclusive' (split-and-recurse)
acceptance: Provably no false-negative on point-in-cube under FP rounding (test with eps-distance edges)
≥10 unit tests including NaN, ±Inf, denormal, overflow
Round-trip E2E: wraps ContinuousCollisionDetectionEngine without behavior change on safe inputs, catches near-edge cases discrete FP misses

units.title: ProgramProofCertificateEngine — orchestrator that produces signed 'this program is safe' verdict
scope: Input: program (G-code or pre-post toolpath) + machine_id + fixture_id + workpiece_geometry
Pipeline: envelope-lookup → IK trajectory → continuous swept-volume → interval-arithmetic distance predicates → cross-engine consensus
Output: ProofCertificate { verdict: 'safe' | 'unsafe' | 'inconclusive', witnesses: [...failed checks], marginsByCheck: { name → µm safety margin }, signedAt, machineId, programHash, accuracyTier }
Performance budget: <1s for 5K-block program, <5s for 50K-block
acceptance: End-to-end on real JM Die program: input program → certificate in <5s

≥15 unit tests including: safe program (verdict safe + positive margins), travel-limit violation (verdict unsafe + axis name in witness), fixture collision (unsafe + intersection point), inconclusive boundary (auto-recurses via interval-arithmetic)
MCP-callable via prism_safety:program_proof_certify
Cert format is schema-versioned + signed (sha256 of program + envelope + engine versions)

units.title: ProgramAutoFixPlannerEngine — when cert fails, pick cheapest valid transform; re-certify until safe or unfixable
scope: Transforms ranked by cost: (1) Z-lift to safe-height, (2) retract-then-rapid-then-plunge, (3) SLERP re-orient (5-axis), (4) feed-rate clamp, (5) setup-split (most expensive)
Greedy planner: pick cheapest transform that addresses the specific witness; re-run cert; iterate until verdict=safe OR no transform applies → report 'unfixable, requires human'
Fixed-point detection: stop after 8 iterations to bound runtime
acceptance: Z-collision → Z-lift fix → re-certified safe (round-trip E2E test)
Travel-limit overshoot → feed-clamp fix → safe
Tank-wall collision in WEDM → setup-split or unfixable verdict (depends on geometry)
≥12 unit tests covering each transform + composition + unfixable + fixed-point
MCP-callable via prism_safety:program_proof_autofix

units.title: Pre-emit gate — wire the certificate into G-code emitter pipelines so no program is emitted without verdict:safe
scope: Hook into: LathePrintProgramEmitterEngine, all PostProcessorPipeline finalize steps, WEDM program emit
Gate behavior: cert.verdict=safe → emit; verdict=unsafe → auto-fix attempt → re-cert → emit; unfixable → reject + report
Bypass: PRISM_PROGRAM_PROOF_BYPASS=1 (logged to state/shared/program-proof-bypasses.jsonl, never silent)
User-facing: every emitted program carries a `// PRISM-PROOF: <cert-sha>` comment header
acceptance: Lathe emit path gated end-to-end (round-trip test: unsafe program → blocked, auto-fix retried, safe emit)
WEDM emit gated end-to-end
Bypass works AND is logged with caller + reason
User-receivable program ALWAYS carries the cert header

units.title: WEDM end-to-end pilot (charlie-domain proof-of-concept) — run on 3 real JM Die wire programs, demonstrate auto-fix
scope: Pick 3 real wire programs from JM DIE/CNC WIRE/ archive (taper cut, fine-finish multi-pass, thick stack)
Run U-PP03 cert; record verdict, witnesses, margins
If unsafe: run U-PP04 auto-fix; record transforms applied
Final report: state/shared/program-proof/WEDM-PILOT-RESULTS.md with per-program verdict + auto-fix trace
acceptance: 3 real programs run through the gate
Per-program report includes upper-head clearance margin (µm), U-V offset cone, tank-wall margin, wire-break risk score
≥1 program demonstrates a real auto-fix transform (Z-lift or feed-clamp), not just pass-through

p2_topology_layer.rationale: Strictly additive over P0 — P0 ships first with metric/geometric proofs; P2 adds topological proofs that catch the rare class of bugs that metric checks miss (knots, anti-podal singularities, bottleneck routing, sheaf-cohomology cross-engine consensus). Each P2 unit is independent — no inter-dependency.

units.title: TopologicalEnvelopeAnalyzerEngine — persistent homology + Morse theory on machine-envelope SDF
scope: Compute persistent homology (H_0 connected components, H_1 loops) of each JM Die machine envelope SDF
Morse decomposition: catalog critical points (saddle points = bottleneck-pose-pairs where safety margin is locally minimal)
Output: per-machine bottleneck-point map, queryable by toolpath
Pure-JS Vietoris-Rips up to dim-1 (sufficient subset, <5KB, no GUDHI dependency)
acceptance: Returns ≥3 bottleneck points for each of 3 spanning machines (Hurco mill, Okuma lathe, GFAgie WEDM)
U-PP04 auto-fix planner consumes the bottleneck map and demonstrates ≥20% shorter path-length on test program vs greedy Z-lift
≥10 unit tests including: empty SDF (degenerate), single-point SDF, multi-component SDF (verify H_0 count), toroidal envelope (verify H_1 nontrivial)

units.title: ConfigSpaceReebGraphEngine — Reeb-graph decomposition of 5-axis C-space, detects anti-podal singularities
scope: Build Reeb graph of the 5-axis C-space (XYZ × ABC torus) parametrized by toolpath progress
Detect anti-podal singularities (wrist flips, ABC rollover at ±180°) as Reeb-graph branch points
Provide SLERP detour that is provably topologically valid (doesn't cross the singular set)
Replaces U-PP04's heuristic SLERP fix with a Reeb-graph-aware planner
acceptance: Detects all 3 anti-podal singularities in a known-bad 5-axis test program (DMG 5-axis mill, A-axis flip near pole)
Re-planned path is collision-free AND continuous (no orientation discontinuity)
Round-trip with U-PP03 cert: original program verdict=unsafe (singularity-cross), re-planned verdict=safe
≥10 unit tests including: no-singularity-case (passthrough), single-singularity (detour), double-singularity (multi-segment detour)

units.title: WEDMWireKnotInvariantEngine — Alexander polynomial of wire path, catches link-with-workpiece class
scope: Charlie-domain (wire EDM specialist)
Compute Alexander polynomial of the wire-path curve (closed by upper-head → start, lower-head → start virtual closure)
Detect non-trivial knot invariant ⇒ wire effectively links with workpiece hole/cavity ⇒ unphysical wire-break required
Catches the stacked-die-program class missed by purely metric geometric checks (~5-10% of real-world WEDM bugs per charlie tribal corpus)
acceptance: Detects link-with-workpiece on synthetic test: wire path that threads a through-hole vs one that doesn't
Alexander polynomial = 1 (trivial knot) for safe wire paths; non-trivial polynomial for linked paths
Integration test: feeds verdict into U-PP03 cert as witness 'wire-knot-invariant-violation' with the polynomial as evidence
≥10 unit tests including: unknot (trivial), trefoil (3_1 knot — should detect), figure-eight, Hopf-link (2-component link)
Respects charlie refuse_list — does NOT inline spark-erosion / pulse-energy constants

units.title: SheafCohomologyMergeEngine — rigorous cross-engine cert verdict consensus via sheaf cohomology
scope: Model the 17 collision/envelope/kinematic engine outputs as sections of a sheaf on the toolpath-segment graph
Compute the first cohomology class H^1 — non-zero ⇒ local engine verdicts are LOCALLY consistent but GLOBALLY contradictory (obstruction to global section)
Replaces U-PP03's 'all engines must vote safe' (too strict) with 'sheaf section exists' (provably-coherent merge)
Reduces U-PP03 false-positive rate (engines disagreeing on edge geometry but each locally correct)
acceptance: Catches synthetic-contradiction case: 3 engines disagree pairwise but each pair is consistent (Mayer-Vietoris obstruction)
On a corpus of 50 known-safe JM Die programs, U-PP03 with sheaf merge drops false-positive rate by ≥30% vs intersection vote
≥10 unit tests including: trivial sheaf (all engines agree → H^1=0 → safe), contradiction-pair (H^1≠0 → conflict report), 3-way contradiction
Pure-JS implementation (cohomology over finite simplicial complex is ~200 LOC linear algebra)

psn_synergy.leg_engines: U-PP03 cert orchestrator IS the unified PSN-leg-7 entry for program safety
psn_synergy.leg_algorithms: U-PP02 interval arithmetic adds the safe-predicate primitive (Moore 1966)
psn_synergy.leg_formulas: Reuses Minkowski sum, GJK distance, BVH, swept-volume from existing formula registry
psn_synergy.leg_nn_gnn: U-PP04 auto-fix planner is a candidate for RL fine-tune via the new PSN autonomy loop (cheap-transform-first policy learned from reward = (1 if cert.verdict==safe else 0) * (1 / transform_cost))

deferred_aspirations: Per-machine laser-interferometer characterization (Renishaw ballbar + XL-80) to lift accuracy_tier from 'manufacturer-spec' (~25-50µm) to 'interferometer-cal' (sub-µm). Requires capital purchase + per-machine calibration day. NOT in scope for MS0.
